content.user_title: Improve Go Code With Best Practices
content.value_statement: Go projects can drift into weak types, unclear interfaces, and inconsistent error handling. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused guidance for idiomatic Go design, errors, and logging.
actual_capabilities: Recommends custom domain types to prevent invalid states.
Shows how to define narrow Go interfaces for behavior contracts.
Demonstrates enum-style constants with explicit default handling.
Explains functional options for flexible constructor design.
Covers error wrapping and structured logging with standard Go patterns.
limitations: Does not run Go tests or formatting tools by itself.
Does not cover concurrency, generics, modules, or build pipelines in depth.
Examples are guidance snippets and may need project-specific adaptation.
Does not infer team standards unless the user provides that context.

use_cases.title: Refactor Domain Models
use_cases.description: Identify weak primitive types and replace them with clearer domain concepts.

use_cases.title: Review Go Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Check interfaces, constructors, error handling, and logging for consistent Go style.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Coding Sessions
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code focused rules before editing Go files.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Go File
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Go file for type safety, clear interfaces, error wrapping, and structured logging. Explain each suggestion clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Domain Types
prompt_templates.prompt: Find primitive values that represent domain concepts. Suggest Go types and method names that make invalid states harder to create.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Constructors
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design pass for configuration-heavy code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these constructors and configuration paths. Recommend functional options only where they reduce call-site complexity.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Service Boundaries
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this Go package boundary. Evaluate interfaces, returned structs, error chains, and logging fields for maintainable service design.

output_examples.input: Review a package that uses plain strings for user IDs and order IDs.
output: Suggest distinct domain types for each identifier.
Explain how compile-time checks reduce accidental mixing.
List migration steps for affected function signatures.

output_examples.input: Improve error handling around an external service call.
output: Recommend preserving the original error chain.
Add context that names the failed operation.
Avoid hiding errors behind generic messages.

output_examples.input: Review logging in a widget creation workflow.
output: Recommend structured fields for component, name, and identifier.
Use debug logs for lifecycle details.
Avoid logging sensitive values without a clear need.

best_practices: Provide real Go files or clear package context before asking for refactors.
Ask for tradeoffs before applying patterns to small packages.
Validate suggested changes with project tests and formatting tools.
anti_patterns: Applying every pattern to trivial code without a design reason.
Replacing project conventions without checking team standards.
Treating short examples as complete production implementations.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps review and write Go code using type safety, focused interfaces, error handling, and structured logging patterns.

faq.question: Does it write complete Go applications?
faq.answer: No. It provides language-specific guidance and examples for Go design and review tasks.

faq.question: Can it review existing Go code?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the relevant files and ask for recommendations based on the included Go practices.

faq.question: Does it run gofmt or tests?
faq.answer: No. The AI tool using the skill may run tools only when you ask and the environment allows it.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is it only for advanced Go users?
faq.answer: No. It includes simple examples, but advanced users can apply the patterns across package boundaries.
